clue.text: Pat is generous lender

definitions.meaning: a pat is a gentle, light stroke of the hand
someone easily persuaded to hand over money

explanation.definitionFit: A gentle pat is a light contact, and a person who readily lends cash is an easy mark; the phrase covers both senses.

clue.text: Fibre is eaten by Sarah

indicators.note: the word is goes inside the name, as food goes into the eater

parts.note: Sal is a familiar short form of Sarah

explanation.surface: A woman named Sarah is seen chewing on some fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a stiff plant fibre used for rope and matting.

clue.text: Hamlet's rude man, a distant relative

definitions.meaning: Gray's Elegy speaks of the rude forebears of the hamlet who sleep in the churchyard, a village's unlettered ancestors
an ancestor several generations back

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet' is not Shakespeare's prince but a village, as in Thomas Gray's Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancestor from long ago is a relative far back in the family tree.

clue.text: Start to tour small island in large continent; this?

definitions.text: Start to tour small island in large continent; this?

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word tour is taken
the small island is placed inside the continent's name

parts.note: Asia is the largest continent
the Isle of Man, a small island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A traveller begins a tour of a small island lying off a huge continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasmania is a small island state lying off the Australian continent, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Divorced some time between Thursday and Tuesday?

definitions.meaning: no longer married

definitions.text: some time between Thursday and Tuesday?
definitions.meaning: the days running from Thursday forward to Tuesday skip the midweek day, so they are not-Wednesday

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as UN-WED: going forward from Thursday to Tuesday you never reach Wednesday.
explanation.definitionFit: Divorced people are no longer married, so they are single again, not wedded.

clue.text: Cheery pub redeveloped in extraordinary shape

indicators.note: redeveloping a pub rebuilds it, so the letters of the words are rebuilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A jolly pub is rebuilt into a building of a very odd shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-dimensional analogue of a cube is a geometric shape unlike anything in ordinary space.

clue.text: Start of honeymoon to which critics regularly invited

definitions.meaning: the wedding evening, which begins the honeymoon
the opening performance of a play, attended by reviewers

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a newly married couple's first evening and a show's premiere for the press.

clue.text: Splendid end to the music

definitions.meaning: excellent, very good
the Italian word written on a score where the piece finishes

explanation.definitionFit: The word means excellent, and in printed music marks the place where a piece ends.

clue.text: Wicked princess overcomes a head of state

indicators.note: the princess's name goes over and around the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: Regan is one of King Lear's cruel daughters

explanation.surface: An evil princess defeats a nation's ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald Reagan was President of the United States, a head of state.

clue.text: What's best to sleep in after night on the tiles?

definitions.text: What's best to sleep in after night on the tiles?

parts.words: What's best to sleep in after night on the tiles?
parts.note: a tomcat out all night on the rooftops would need nightwear; the phrase for this also means the very best thing

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what to wear to bed after a night out partying.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'night on the tiles' is a night out carousing, from cats roaming the roofs; the answer is slang for something excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is old slang for the very best, and literally would be a feline's nightwear.

clue.text: Incident confused with riot leads to ban

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters of the two words are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A muddled incident and a riot lead the authorities to impose a ban.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two fodder words and 'leads to' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An interdiction is an official prohibition or order forbidding something.

clue.text: Poet, fallible, broken first by love then by start of sex?

indicators.note: the split word is then broken again by a second letter
the word for fallible is split open first by the letter for love

parts.note: to err is human, so human means fallible
love is zero in tennis, written O

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word sex is taken

explanation.surface: A flawed poet is ruined first by love and then by the beginnings of sex.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes in after the H of HUMAN, giving HOUMAN; S then goes in after the U.
explanation.definitionFit: A. E. Housman was an English poet, author of A Shropshire Lad.

clue.text: Feeble complaint about lack of policing

definitions.meaning: poor, of little worth
read literally, a grumble that there are too few police officers about

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cop' is British slang for worth or value as well as for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for something of little value or use, here weak and feeble.

clue.text: Heat regularly opens most of cluster of flowers

indicators.note: every other letter of the word opens is taken, at regular intervals
the final letter is removed from the word for a flower cluster

parts.note: a truss is a compact cluster of flowers on one stalk

explanation.surface: Warm weather routinely brings out most of a bunch of blossoms.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on heat is the period of sexual receptivity in female mammals, known by the technical term.

clue.text: A hundred are locked into vigil

indicators.note: the two pieces are placed inside the word for vigil

parts.note: a wake is a watch kept over a body
the are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated a
pent means shut up or confined

explanation.surface: A hundred people are shut in during an all-night watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A hundred' is the definition: in old England a hundred was a county division, called by another name in the northern counties.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a subdivision of some English shires, the equivalent of the southern hundred.

clue.text: Turn book's pages for Tom

definitions.meaning: to leaf through a book with one's digit
the tiny hero of the folk tale, Tom of finger-size

explanation.definitionFit: To flick through pages is to use the digit, and Tom of the fairy tale is named after it.

clue.text: Side of river has current, say, that is negotiable

parts.note: a river's bank is its side

indicators.note: say signals that the word for current is heard, not seen, and spelt another way

parts.note: a draught is a current of air

explanation.surface: A riverbank has a current that, apparently, can be bargained with.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank draft is a cheque drawn by a bank, a negotiable instrument that can be transferred.

clue.text: Book prostitute to go to war zone

parts.note: moll is old slang for a prostitute or gangster's girl
Flanders, in Belgium, was a great battleground of the First World War

explanation.surface: A prostitute is booked to travel to a war zone.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe's novel about a woman's misadventures is a famous book.

clue.text: Lancer in line army trained in part of Ireland

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are placed inside the Irish county's name

parts.note: Cavan is a county in Ireland

indicators.note: training reshapes, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier with a lance serves in a line regiment trained in an Irish county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' turns L and ARMY into ALRYM, which goes inside CAVAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A lancer was a mounted soldier carrying a lance, so a horse soldier.

clue.text: Extremely unpleasing shape, showing principally this?

definitions.text: Extremely unpleasing shape, showing principally this?

indicators.note: the extreme letters, first and last, of the word unpleasing

parts.note: the lines of something are its outline or shape

indicators.note: the principal, first, letter of the word showing

explanation.surface: A displeasing form shows mainly one quality.
explanation.definitionFit: An unpleasing shape shows plainness of appearance, which is the whole clue's sense.

clue.text: Refreshment room that employs Shakers?

parts.note: not the religious sect but cocktail shakers, used in a bar where mixed drinks are served

explanation.surface: A tearoom hires members of a religious sect.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital S makes 'Shakers' look like the American religious sect; it is the bar equipment for mixing drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar room in a hotel where mixed drinks are shaken and served.

clue.text: Poor Clare, alas, not spiritual

indicators.note: an exclamation of distress, read as a sign that the letters have come to grief and been jumbled

explanation.surface: A nun of the Poor Clares, sadly, lacks spirituality.
explanation.walkthrough: A Poor Clare is a nun of the Franciscan order founded by St Clare.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporeal means bodily, of the physical world, the opposite of spiritual.

clue.text: Silently getting message at the front to arrest one pair

indicators.note: arresting means holding, so the word for at the front holds the other pieces

parts.note: leading means in front
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A message arrives first telling police to arrest two people.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading lips lets a deaf person understand speech without hearing it.

clue.text: Authorised after endless request to be transferred

indicators.note: after means the word for authorised follows the other piece
the final letter is removed from the word for request

parts.note: to ask is to request
signed means authorised by signature

explanation.surface: Permission is granted after an unfinished request to be moved.
explanation.definitionFit: Property assigned to another has been legally transferred to them.

clue.text: In little room, 'amper a poor girl

indicators.note: the dropped-aitch word is placed inside the word for a little room

parts.note: a cell is a small room
hamper with the H dropped, as a Cockney might say it; hinder likewise loses its H

explanation.surface: In a cramped room someone hampers a poor girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''amper' shows the dropped H, so its synonym hinder drops its H too, giving INDER.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy-tale heroine is the classic poor girl, a drudge before her rise.

clue.text: Check on dog as horses jump

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
to vet is to check

explanation.surface: Someone checks a dog while horses leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A curvet is a leap in which a horse raises its forelegs and springs forward.

clue.text: Sadly perish before urban area achieves fully regular form

indicators.note: sadly here signals that the word is mixed up

parts.note: a city is an urban area

explanation.surface: Sadly, the countryside dies when the town spreads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' turns PERISH into SPHERI.
explanation.definitionFit: The quality of being a perfect ball, which is the most regular of forms.

clue.text: Staff officer's marking note on pair of drums

parts.note: staff officers wear coloured tabs on their collars
la is a note in sol-fa

explanation.surface: A staff officer marks a note on a couple of drums.
explanation.definitionFit: The tabla is a pair of small Indian hand drums.

clue.text: Meeting an unknown Venetian?

parts.note: a rendezvous with a stranger, punning on the Venetian kind of window shade

explanation.surface: Someone has a rendezvous with a stranger from Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: A Venetian is also a kind of window blind, so a date with one is the meeting arranged with a stranger.
explanation.definitionFit: A date with someone you have never met is the name for a romantic meeting with a stranger.

clue.text: I am getting your message, and agree entirely

definitions.meaning: taken literally, an acknowledgement that someone is informing me
a colloquial exclamation of emphatic agreement

explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation literally says one is being informed and idiomatically means emphatic agreement.

clue.text: A summer concert for millions?

parts.note: pro means in favour of
M stands for million

explanation.surface: A summer concert is put on for the masses.
explanation.definitionFit: The Proms are the BBC's annual summer concert season, and one concert is a prom.

clue.text: Extra drama around midweek — that creates a buzz

indicators.note: around turns both words back to front

parts.note: a bye is an extra in cricket
Noh is classical Japanese drama
the middle letters of the word week, the two central letters

explanation.surface: Additional theatre around the middle of the week causes excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns BYE and NOH into HONEYB; the middle of WEEK gives EE.
explanation.definitionFit: The insect hums as it flies, so it literally makes a buzzing noise.

clue.text: Bloke I found in efficient library

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person or chap

indicators.note: the letter I is found within the word for efficient

parts.note: a lean organisation is efficient, without waste

explanation.surface: A man finds himself working in an efficient library.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bodleian is the main research library of Oxford University.

clue.text: Girl to do away with — almost time for sorcerer

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

indicators.note: the final letter is dropped from the word for doing away with

parts.note: to abolish is to do away with

explanation.surface: A girl plans to dispose of someone just before the sorcerer arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: A diabolist is one who deals with the devil, a practitioner of black magic.

clue.text: Musical, sadly old, sung badly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A musical, sadly dated, is poorly sung.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' looks like an anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'badly' is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Loesser's Broadway show about New York gamblers is a famous musical.

clue.text: Pleased to entertain queen with unreliable fortune

indicators.note: entertaining a guest means taking them in, so the word for pleased holds the other piece

parts.note: cheered means made glad

explanation.surface: Someone is happy to host a queen whose luck is unsteady.
explanation.definitionFit: A chequered career or history is one with ups and downs, of mixed fortune.

clue.text: Criminal at first is given thirty days, possessing old rifle

indicators.note: the first letter of the word criminal is taken

parts.note: has means is given or possesses

indicators.note: the month's abbreviation holds the letter for old

parts.note: September has thirty days, abbreviated Sept

explanation.surface: A criminal is sentenced to thirty days for carrying an old gun.
explanation.definitionFit: The chassepot was a French breech-loading rifle of the 1860s.

clue.text: During housework hanging around in confusion

indicators.note: the reversed word sits during, inside, the work word

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is work done on one's own house

indicators.note: around turns the tapestry word back to front

parts.note: an arras is a wall hanging, a tapestry

explanation.surface: Things hang about in a mess while the housework is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns ARRAS into SARRA, which goes inside DIY.
explanation.definitionFit: Disarray is a state of disorder or muddle.

clue.text: Day in Rome that is short

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut from the Latin phrase

parts.note: id est is Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A day in Rome, that is, is brief.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ides were days in the Roman calendar, the 15th or 13th of the month.

clue.text: Lace underwear not very supporting all round

indicators.note: the word for supporting goes all round the other piece

parts.note: shoring means propping up, supporting

indicators.note: very is abbreviated V, and that letter is dropped

parts.note: a vest is an undergarment

explanation.surface: Lace lingerie gives little support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not very' takes V from VEST, leaving EST, which SHORING surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A bootlace or shoelace is a lace for fastening footwear.

clue.text: "Sweet hay hath no fellow": a decisive factor

definitions.meaning: a line spoken by Bottom the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream
the crucial point or final consideration

explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's comedy Bottom, wearing an ass's head, says this; so it is his speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both the decisive consideration and literally a line said by Bottom.

clue.text: Line through Mars city

indicators.note: the letter runs through, inside, the god's name

parts.note: Ares is the Greek counterpart of the Roman god Mars

explanation.surface: A line passes across the planet Mars to a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Arles is a city in Provence, southern France.

clue.text: Fairy ring found by gypsy

parts.note: tinker is an old word for a travelling gypsy
a ring is the sound of a bell

explanation.surface: A fairy ring is discovered by a wandering traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Pan's companion is a famous fairy.

clue.text: Officer rose, suppressing one expression of surprise

indicators.note: suppressing means holding down, so the word for rose holds the other pieces

parts.note: a brier is a wild rose
I is the Roman numeral for one
gad is a mild exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: An officer stood up, stifling a cry of astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigadier is a senior army officer.

clue.text: Article to add to casserole?

indicators.note: the article and the word to are added after the cooking pot

parts.note: a casserole is a cooking pot

explanation.surface: Something to throw into a stew.
explanation.definitionFit: A potato is a typical item added to a casserole, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Castle is prepared for Greek play

indicators.note: preparing something gets it ready by rearranging, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A castle is made ready for a Greek tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Euripides wrote the tragedy about the wife who dies for her husband.

clue.text: Kill second figure in plane — I escaped

indicators.note: the letter I escapes, so it is removed

parts.note: a triangle is a plane figure

explanation.surface: A second person is killed on a plane, while I got away.
explanation.definitionFit: To strangle someone is to kill them by choking.

clue.text: Walter's not quite correct to drink beer

indicators.note: drinking takes the beer inside
the last letter is dropped from the word for correct

parts.note: right means correct
ale is beer

explanation.surface: Walter is not entirely right to drink some beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Raleigh was the Elizabethan courtier and explorer, so it is Walter's surname.

clue.text: Last carpet tile replaced in blocks

indicators.note: replacing a tile puts things in new positions, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The final carpet tile is put down anew.
explanation.definitionFit: Block letters are upper-case letters, written in blocks.

clue.text: Allow forward across road

indicators.note: the word for forward lies across, around, the road

parts.note: pert means forward or cheeky
the M1 motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: Someone is allowed to cross a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to give someone leave or permission to do something is to let them do it.

clue.text: Noisily I establish support — quietly I directed the flow

parts.note: P stands for piano, quietly
led means directed
a river is a flowing stream

explanation.surface: A loud worker builds foundations, while a quiet one guides the stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that drives piles into the ground noisily to support buildings.

clue.text: He joins ministers before God

indicators.note: before means the ministers come first

parts.note: the cabinet is the senior group of ministers
God is the Maker

explanation.surface: A man joins the government ministers before God.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who makes fine furniture joins pieces of wood together.

clue.text: Depart for Arabia in pilgrim ship

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the words pilgrim ship

explanation.surface: A pilgrim sets out on a ship to Arabia.
explanation.definitionFit: Army slang from Arabic meaning go away, so an Arab's word for depart.

clue.text: Whip has nothing to say

indicators.note: to say signals the word for nothing is spoken, and spelt another way

parts.note: nowt is northern English for nothing

explanation.surface: The whip has nothing to say for itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A knout is a Russian whip formerly used for flogging.

clue.text: Admired figure admitting deception?

definitions.meaning: an idol, a person widely revered
read as two words, a confession that I trick people

explanation.walkthrough: Split as I CON, the word is the speaker owning up to trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: A revered person is an idol of popular culture, the modern sense of the word.

clue.text: Ornament of king found in dig

indicators.note: the king's letter is found inside the word for dig

parts.note: to till is to dig the soil
R stands for rex, king

explanation.surface: A king's ornament is discovered in an excavation.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a trill is an ornament, a rapid alternation of notes.

clue.text: Two things casino provides — in its restaurant?

definitions.text: Two things casino provides — in its restaurant?

parts.words: Two things casino provides — in its restaurant?
parts.note: a casino offers gambling and tokens; put together they name thin fried potato slices served with roast pheasant

explanation.surface: Wonders what food a gambling house might serve.
explanation.walkthrough: The two things are a game and chips; together they name crisps served with roast game birds in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin fried potato crisps traditionally served with roast game birds.

clue.text: Ripped at the edges, almost sumptuous hat

indicators.note: the word for ripped forms the edges around the other piece

parts.note: torn means ripped

indicators.note: the last letter is cut from the word for sumptuous

parts.note: rich means sumptuous

explanation.surface: A nearly luxurious hat is torn round the brim.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricorn is a hat with the brim turned up on three sides.

clue.text: Writer not returning to walled city

parts.note: Chester is an English city famous for its Roman walls

indicators.note: returning means the word not is read backwards

explanation.surface: A writer will not go back to a walled city.
explanation.definitionFit: G. K. Chesterton was an English writer, creator of Father Brown.

clue.text: Thoroughly wet newts pair off

indicators.note: off here means gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two drenched newts are leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain-swept means battered and soaked by rain, so thoroughly wet.
